Gemini writes your scripts

16 November 2026 · Reading time: 4 minutes · Audio in the app: 5 minutes. Listening to the briefing is part of Sapaude Pro.

Google has made the Gemini side panel in Apps Script generally available. Describe a repetitive task in plain language, and Gemini writes the script.

Sapaude retells the story in its own words. The source is below. Publisher: Sapaude.

In three points

Three points, in this order: what the source shows, where that claim stops, and what to check next.

  1. Google announced general availability on 16 November 2026, following a public beta earlier this year. The panel sits in the Apps Script editor behind Sheets, Docs, Slides and Forms.
  2. Gemini proposes code block by block, and you accept or reject each block before saving. Fix errors in the Execution log explains a failure in plain language and suggests a fix.
  3. Scripts run with the user's existing permissions and standard OAuth consent. Admins control access by organizational unit or group. The rollout started on 12 November and can take up to 15 days.

From description to working script

Google Apps Script is built into Sheets, Docs, Slides and Forms under Extensions > Apps Script. On 16 November 2026 Google made the Gemini side panel in the editor generally available, following a public beta earlier this year. According to Google, anyone in an organization can now create, customize and troubleshoot scripts in plain language, with no coding experience required.

Google's examples: creating Calendar events from urgent Gmail messages, pulling and cleaning real-time data, or turning Sheets tables into formatted Docs reports. Gemini understands the files across the open Apps Script project, and users can keep chatting to add capabilities such as time-based triggers.

Review block by block, fix in one click

Gemini's suggestions land directly in the editor. Multi-block changes can be accepted or rejected one block at a time, or all at once with Accept All and Reject All, before saving. If a script fails at runtime, Fix errors in the Execution log has Gemini diagnose the problem, explain it in plain language and insert a proposed fix.

The panel opens automatically on new scripts at script.google.com or script.new. In existing projects it sits behind the Ask Gemini spark icon in the top right corner of the editor.

Your permissions, your admin's rules

Google stresses that broader access does not mean less oversight. Scripts run natively in Workspace with the user's existing permissions and standard OAuth consent. Admins keep the existing Apps Script service settings and generative AI controls in the Admin console. They can manage access by organizational unit or group, restrict data access through OAuth app controls and external URL allowlists, and monitor activity in Drive and OAuth audit logs.

The responsibility stays where it was: a generated script can do whatever the account running it can do. Accepting a block means keeping that code, not that anyone has checked it.

Rollout and plans

The gradual rollout for Rapid Release and Scheduled Release domains started on 12 November 2026, and Google says the feature can take up to 15 days to become visible. It is available on Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, the AI Expanded Access add-on, Google AI Pro for Education, and the consumer Google AI Pro and Ultra plans.

What you can do

Try one small automation in a sheet you already use, such as cleaning a single column, and read each block before you accept it. If the spark icon is missing, the rollout may not have reached you yet, or your admin has switched the feature off.

In the app, the same story is also told shorter and in more detail, matched to your level.

Source: Google Workspace Updates. Published: 16 November 2026.
